With `ex` bound to the default IRI, `doc.entity(<that IRI>)` gets the identifier `ex[""]`, spelled `ex:`. An empty local part after a prefix stays legal under production [52], so an IRI equal to a prefixed namespace's IRI is that prefix's name (spec 3 section 4.3).

In a bundle that rebinds the prefix `ex`, which the document binds to the default IRI, asserting the empty local part of that default raises `ProvExceptionInvalidQualifiedName` matching `declare a prefix`. An identifier equal to the default namespace's IRI is rejected, and a prefix the bundle rebinds does not spell it (#473, spec 3 section 4.3). Later audit: before anyone proposes removing this test in favour of test_qnames.py::test_identifier_equal_to_the_default_namespace_iri_is_rejected, have a verifier plant a fault that limits the early raise in `NamespaceManager._reconcile_qualified_name` to the scope's own default, because the classifier and the judge expected only this test to fail under it.

`doc.entity()` of the default namespace's IRI as text, and of the empty local part in that namespace, each raises `ProvExceptionInvalidQualifiedName` with the stated detail, and no namespace is registered. An identifier equal to the default namespace's IRI has no qualified-name form, and the model mints no prefix for it (#473, spec 3 section 4.3, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

A literal whose datatype uses the prefix `zz` for an IRI the document binds elsewhere is stored with the datatype under `zz_1`, and the document survives the round trip in every target. A datatype whose prefix clashes with a declared one takes a free prefix, so the literal and the declaration agree (#615, spec 3 section 4.2).

Asserting an attribute whose literal datatype is a name in another default namespace than the document's raises `ProvExceptionInvalidQualifiedName` with the sentence that names the local part, the namespace and the instruction to declare a prefix. A name in a default namespace that is not the default in scope is rejected with one sentence (#473, spec 3 section 4.2, docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md).

A literal whose datatype is in an undeclared namespace `zz` registers it, so the registered prefixes are `ex` and `zz`, and the document survives the round trip in every target. A datatype in a namespace nothing declared registers that namespace when it is asserted, so every writer declares it (#615, spec 3 section 4.2).

The test asserts that `ProvRecord._literal_in_scope(Literal("1", XSD_INT), XSD_INT)` returns the same `Literal` object, which pins an identity through a private method. It passes with the `xsd` and `prov` early return removed, because the fall-through through `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname` returns the same literal when the held namespace equals the datatype's. The verifier removed that early return and the whole suite still gave 5307 passed, 13 skipped and 1 xfailed, so no test sees the shortcut. Its input also never reaches the method through a public call, because `ProvRecord._convert_typed_literal` turns `Literal("1", XSD_INT)` into the int `1`. The contract behind it is that a built-in datatype is held as it is and registers no namespace (the docstring of `ProvRecord._literal_in_scope`, from #615). The maintainer accepted the classifier's `rewrite` and the test does not change yet. The planned rewrite is a row of test_qnames.py::test_literal_datatype_registers_its_namespace with `Literal("01", XSD_INT)` expecting the prefixes `{"ex"}`, an input a public call delivers to `ProvRecord._literal_in_scope`.

A document that declares the prefix `ex` and holds a bundle `ex:bundle` with the entity `ex:e1` in it survives the round trip in every target, and the entity keeps its identifier. A bundle reads the document's prefix declarations and declares none of its own (#449, spec 3 section 4.1).

A document that declares a prefix called `default` and uses it in an identifier, an attribute name and value, a datatype and a relation survives the round trip in every target. PROV-JSON keys the default namespace as `default`, so a prefix of that name must be renamed on writing (#518).

A document prefix called `default` used in a bundle, and a second bundle with its own prefix `default`, survive the round trip in every target. PROV-JSON keys the default namespace as `default`, so a prefix of that name must be renamed on writing, also inside a bundle (#518, #573).

`provn_bare_representation()` on an empty local part in a default namespace raises `ProvException` matching `prefix`, and on an empty local part under the prefix `ex` returns `ex:`. A name with an empty local part and no prefix has no PROV-N spelling, while `prefix:` with an empty local part stays legal under production [52] (spec 3 section 4.3, 3.2.1 HISTORY entry on empty local parts).
